page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture featuring an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The server provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, but provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

The underlying AMD hardware supports specialized instructions, including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI for cryptographic speedups, alongside AVX, BMI2, ADX, and FMA for mathematical routines. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong single-core processor performance in stress-ng evaluations and high memory efficiency in PassMark scoring. Multi-threaded benchmark results position the server in the middle performance tier across PassMark CPU (35,962.63), Geekbench multi-core (11,323.0), and Redis SET operations (31.19 million ops/sec).

A key tradeoff lies in uncached memory write operations, which record a lower bandwidth of 18.87 GB/sec. However, small model LLM text generation shows strong execution at 287.51 tokens per second. Given its core-focused hardware profile and standard network throughput, ecs.c7a.8xlarge offers practical resource density for software compilation, web serving infrastructure, database tasks, and lightweight artificial intelligence workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with a KVM hypervisor, it features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 64.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware security and bit manipulation features include AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and standard AVX extensions. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core compute performance and high PassMark memory efficiency, alongside average multi-threaded CPU output and static web serving throughput. Notable trade-offs include uncached write memory bandwidth bottlenecks and a complete lack of bundled local storage. Providing an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, ecs.c7a.8xlarge delivers cost-effective core density well suited for web hosting, software compilation, database tasks, and lightweight AI text generation.
